mainTopic: The end of רבן גמליאל's משנה on explaining פסח, מצה, and מרור and beginning הלל, and the גמרא on lifting the מצה and מרור and whether a blind person must say the הגדה
overview: This amud finishes the משנה of רבן גמליאל and begins the גמרא on it. רבן גמליאל teaches that at the סדר you must say and explain three things: פסח, מצה, and מרור, each with its reason and a פסוק. The משנה adds that in every generation a person must see himself as if he personally left מצרים. Therefore we must praise ה׳, and we begin הלל. בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about how much הלל to say before the meal, and רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא give two versions of the closing ברכת הגאולה. In the גמרא, רבא requires saying 'ואותנו הוציא משם' and teaches that we lift the מצה and מרור but not the meat. רב אחא בר יעקב rules that a blind person is exempt from the הגדה, based on the word 'זה'. The גמרא tests this against the blind sages רב יוסף and רב ששת, who led the הגדה themselves, and it ends by showing that the word 'זה' in the הגדה is needed for its plain meaning, so it does not exclude the blind. Finally, the גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'לפיכך אנחנו חייבים' to open the next discussion.

steps.title: Three things must be said at the סדר
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל rules that anyone who does not say these three things on פסח has not fulfilled his obligation. The three are פסח, מצה, and מרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Whoever did not say] these three things on פסח has not fulfilled his obligation. They are: the פסח offering, מצה, and מרור.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה, continuing רבן גמליאל's words, states a rule: at the סדר you must say and explain three specific things, or you have not fulfilled your obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating פסח, מצה, and מרור is not enough here. רבן גמליאל adds a requirement to verbally mention and explain them. The next three steps give the explanation for each one.
steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'רבן גמליאל היה אומר: כל שלא אמר' ('רבן גמליאל would say: Whoever did not say') come right before it. The obligation is about SAYING these three things, not only eating them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הגדה paragraph 'רבן גמליאל היה אומר', which is recited at every סדר.

phrases.english: [whoever did not say] these three things on Passover
phrases.notes: The words 'whoever did not say' come on the previous amud.

phrases.english: has not fulfilled his obligation,
and these are they: the Paschal lamb, matza, and bitter herbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים אֵלּוּ בַּפֶּסַח לֹא יָצָא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבן גמליאל's statement from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must verbally mention and explain פסח, מצה, and מרור at the סדר to fulfill the obligation.

steps.title: Why we have the פסח offering
steps.stepSummary: The פסח is explained: ה׳ passed over the houses of our forefathers in מצרים. A פסוק is brought as support.
steps.simpleTranslation: פסח: because the Omnipresent passed over the houses of our forefathers in Egypt, as it says, 'And you shall say: It is a פסח offering to ה׳, Who passed over…'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the first of the three items. The קרבן פסח is called 'פסח' because ה׳ 'passed over' the Jewish homes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name 'פסח' (passing over) is itself the reason. The פסוק from שמות shows that the Torah ties the offering directly to ה׳ skipping over the Jewish homes during מכת בכורות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the Place': a name for ה׳ (the Omnipresent)
as it is said (introduces a פסוק)
'etc.': the rest of the פסוק continues

phrases.english: Pesach: because the Omnipresent passed over
the houses of our forefathers in Egypt,
as it is said: 'And you shall say: It is a Pesach sacrifice to ה׳'
'Who passed over, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the three items listed in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reason for the פסח is that ה׳ passed over the Jewish homes in מצרים.

steps.title: Why we eat מצה
steps.stepSummary: מצה is explained: our forefathers were redeemed from מצרים so quickly that their dough could not rise. A פסוק is brought as support.
steps.simpleTranslation: מצה: because our forefathers were redeemed from Egypt, as it says, 'And they baked the dough which they took out of Egypt…'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the second item. מצה reminds us of the גאולה (redemption) from מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק explains how מצה connects to the redemption. The Jews were rushed out of מצרים, so their dough had no time to rise and they baked it as מצות. מצה is therefore a symbol of the speed of the גאולה.

phrases.english: Matza: because were redeemed
our forefathers from Egypt,
as it is said: 'And they baked the dough'
'which they took out of Egypt, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַצָּה — עַל שׁוּם שֶׁנִּגְאֲלוּ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second of the three items from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reason for מצה is the hurried redemption from מצרים.

steps.title: Why we eat bitter herbs
steps.stepSummary: מרור is explained: the Egyptians made our forefathers' lives bitter. A פסוק is brought as support.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרור: because the Egyptians embittered the lives of our forefathers in Egypt, as it says, 'And they embittered their lives…'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the third item. The bitter taste of מרור reminds us of the bitter slavery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מרור comes from the same root as 'וימררו' (they embittered). The food recalls the bitterness of the slavery, just as its name recalls the פסוק.

phrases.english: Maror: because the Egyptians embittered
the lives of our forefathers in Egypt,
as it is said: 'And they embittered their lives, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third and final item from step 1, completing רבן גמליאל's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reason for מרור is the bitter slavery in מצרים.
steps.whatToRemember: The three things you must say at the סדר: פסח (ה׳ passed over our houses), מצה (we were redeemed in a hurry), and מרור (our lives were made bitter).

steps.title: Every person must see himself as having left Egypt
steps.stepSummary: In every generation, a person must view himself as if he personally left מצרים. This is learned from the פסוק 'בעבור זה עשה ה׳ לי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: In every generation a person is obligated to see himself as though he left Egypt, as it says: 'And you shall tell your son on that day, saying: Because of this ה׳ did for me when I went out of Egypt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new obligation. You must feel that the יציאת מצרים happened to you personally, not just to your ancestors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the word 'לי' (for me) in the פסוק. Every father in every generation says 'ה׳ did this for ME when I left מצרים', so the Torah treats each person as if he himself was redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: and you shall tell your son (the source of the word הגדה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the heart of the סדר experience. The night is meant to be a personal reliving of the redemption, not a history lesson.

phrases.english: In each and every generation a person is obligated
to view himself
as though he left Egypt,
as it is said: 'And you shall tell your son on that day, saying:'
'Because of this ה׳ did for me'
phrases.notes: The key word is 'לי', meaning 'for me'.

phrases.english: 'when I went out of Egypt.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל דּוֹר וָדוֹר חַיָּיב אָדָם לִרְאוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the three items to a broader personal obligation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each person must view himself as personally redeemed from מצרים, based on the word 'לי' in the פסוק.

steps.title: Therefore we must praise ה׳
steps.stepSummary: Because each of us was personally redeemed, we are obligated to thank and praise ה׳ with nine expressions of praise for all the miracles He did for our forefathers and for us.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore we are obligated to thank, praise, glorify, extol, exalt, honor, bless, revere, and laud the One Who did all these miracles for our forefathers and for us.
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'לפיכך' (therefore) shows the משנה drawing a conclusion. Since we ourselves were redeemed, we must praise ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step builds directly on step 5. Because the miracles were done 'for us' and not only for our forefathers, the praise is our own personal obligation. The long list of praise words shows how much thanks is owed.

phrases.english: Therefore we are obligated
to thank, to praise, to glorify,
to extol, to exalt, to honor,
to bless, to revere, and to laud
the One Who did for our forefathers and for us
all these miracles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion ('therefore') from the personal redemption taught in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because the redemption was ours personally, we owe ה׳ abundant praise.

steps.title: From slavery to freedom, and then הללויה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists what ה׳ did for us, five changes from bad to good, ending with 'and we will say before Him הללויה'. This leads into reciting הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took us out from slavery to freedom, from sorrow to joy, from mourning to a festival, from darkness to great light, and from bondage to redemption. And we will say before Him: הללויה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the miracles we are praising, then opens the way into הלל with the word 'הללויה'. This line sets up the הלל that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair moves from a low state to a high one, showing the full turnaround of the redemption. 'ונאמר לפניו הללויה' turns the obligation to praise into actual praise: the first chapter of הלל, which begins with הללויה.
steps.whatToRemember: The סדר moves from story to praise. We explain פסח, מצה, and מרור, see ourselves as personally redeemed, and therefore praise ה׳ by beginning הלל ('הללויה').

phrases.english: He took us out from slavery to freedom,
from sorrow to joy,
and from mourning to a festival,
and from darkness to a great light,
and from bondage to redemption.
And we will say before Him: Halleluyah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Details the miracles mentioned in step 6 and completes the praise by leading into הלל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The redemption was a complete turnaround from suffering to joy, and our response is to say הללויה and begin הלל.

steps.title: How far into הלל do we go before the meal?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks where one stops reciting הלל at this point in the סדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until where does he say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה just ended with 'and we will say before Him הללויה', so we start הלל. Now it asks how much of הלל we say before the meal. This line sets up the dispute that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not say all of הלל at once on the סדר night. Part comes before the meal and the rest comes after. The question is where to draw the line.

phrases.english: Until where does he recite [הלל]?
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person leading the סדר. The object, הלל, is understood from the previous step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from 'ונאמר לפניו הללויה' by asking how much הלל is said now.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The stopping point of the first part of הלל, said before the meal.

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל on where to stop
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say we stop after the first chapter of הלל ('אם הבנים שמחה'). בית הלל say we stop after the second chapter ('חלמיש למעינו מים').
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: until 'a joyful mother of children'. בית הלל say: until 'the flint into a fountain of water'.
steps.whatsHappening: Two schools answer the question. Each names a different פסוק where we stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אם הבנים שמחה' ends the first chapter of הלל (תהלים קיג). 'חלמיש למעינו מים' ends the second chapter (תהלים קיד), which is about leaving מצרים. So בית הלל include the chapter about יציאת מצרים before the meal.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of הלל, whose view we follow
End of the first chapter of הלל
End of the second chapter, 'בצאת ישראל'

steps.whyThisMatters: We follow בית הלל. That is why at our סדר we say both 'הללויה הללו עבדי ה׳' and 'בצאת ישראל ממצרים' before the meal.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
Until 'a joyful mother of children'.
phrases.notes: תהלים קיג:ט, the end of the first chapter.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
Until 'the flint into a fountain of water'.
phrases.notes: תהלים קיד:ח, the end of 'בצאת ישראל'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי: one chapter. בית הלל: two chapters.

steps.title: Ending with a blessing about redemption: רבי טרפון's version
steps.stepSummary: After this part of הלל, one ends with a ברכה about redemption. רבי טרפון's version is 'אשר גאלנו וגאל את אבותינו ממצרים', and it has no closing 'ברוך אתה ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he concludes with redemption. רבי טרפון says: 'Who redeemed us and redeemed our forefathers from מצרים', and he would not add a closing ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה says this section ends with a ברכה praising ה׳ for redemption. רבי טרפון then gives its wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון's ברכה looks only at the past: ה׳ redeemed us and our forefathers. 'ולא היה חותם' means he did not add a second 'ברוך אתה ה׳' at the end, so it is a short ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Concludes; ends a ברכה with 'ברוך אתה ה׳'
A תנא, a colleague of רבי עקיבא

steps.confusionAlert: 'ולא היה חותם' does not mean he skipped the ברכה. It means his ברכה had no closing line beginning 'ברוך אתה ה׳'.

phrases.english: And he concludes with [a blessing of] redemption.
Rabbi Tarfon says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר גְּאָלָנוּ וְגָאַל אֶת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם,
phrases.english: 'Who redeemed us and redeemed our forefathers from Egypt',
and he would not conclude [with 'Blessed are You, ה׳'].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After stopping הלל, the משנה tells us how to end this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The section ends with ברכת הגאולה. In רבי טרפון's version it is a short ברכה with no closing formula.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא adds a prayer for the future redemption
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא adds a request: just as ה׳ redeemed us, may He bring us to future holidays in peace, with ירושלים rebuilt and the קרבנות restored. The ברכה ends with 'ברוך אתה ה׳ גאל ישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'So too, ה׳ our God and God of our forefathers, bring us to other holidays and festivals that are coming toward us in peace, happy in the building of Your city and joyful in Your service, and there we will eat from the פסחים and from the זבחים, etc.', until 'Blessed are You ה׳, Who redeemed Israel'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a longer version of the ברכה. It adds a prayer for the future and ends with a full closing ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון looked only back at the past. רבי עקיבא also looks forward to the בית המקדש being rebuilt. Because his version is long, it gets a closing 'ברוך אתה ה׳ גאל ישראל'.

keyTerms.meaning: Who redeemed Israel, the closing words of the ברכה

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends here. We say the first two chapters of הלל (like בית הלל), then the ברכה 'אשר גאלנו'. Our הגדה uses רבי עקיבא's longer version, ending 'גאל ישראל'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the exact ברכה we say at the סדר before drinking the second כוס.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
'So too, ה׳ our God and God of our forefathers,'
bring us to other holidays and festivals
that are coming toward us, in peace,
happy in the building of Your city,
and joyful in Your service.

phrases.aramaic: וְנֹאכַל שָׁם (מִן הַפְּסָחִים וּמִן הַזְּבָחִים) כּוּ׳״,
phrases.english: And there we will eat (from the Paschal lambs and from the offerings), etc.,'
phrases.notes: 'כו׳' means the text goes on; the full wording is in our הגדה.

phrases.english: until 'Blessed are You, ה׳, Who redeemed Israel'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רבי טרפון's version with a request for the future and a closing ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכת הגאולה includes a prayer for the future redemption and ends 'ברוך אתה ה׳ גאל ישראל'.

steps.title: רבא: one must say "And He took us out from there"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins. רבא says the הגדה must include 'ואותנו הוציא משם' (and He took US out from there).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: one must say 'and He took us out from there'.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is over and the גמרא starts. רבא requires a specific פסוק to be said, one that includes us personally in the redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on step 5: each person must see himself as having left מצרים. The words 'ואותנו הוציא משם' (דברים ו:כג) say this out loud. ה׳ took out not only our ancestors but us too.

keyTerms.meaning: And He took us out from there

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rava said:
One must say 'and He took us out from there'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first statement in the גמרא. It ties back to the idea that each person was personally redeemed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הגדה must include 'ואותנו הוציא משם'.

steps.title: רבא: lift the מצה and מרור, but not the meat
steps.stepSummary: When saying 'מצה זו' and 'מרור זה', one lifts them to show everyone. One does not lift the meat. In fact, it is wrong to lift it, because it would look like eating קדשים outside the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: מצה must be lifted, and מרור must be lifted. Meat does not need to be lifted. And not only that, but [lifting it] looks like eating קדשים outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא teaches a practical rule for when we explain פסח, מצה, ומרור. We lift the מצה and the מרור, but not the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting an item points to it as the subject being explained. The meat on our table today is not a קרבן פסח. Lifting it as 'this is the פסח' would make it look like we are treating it as a קרבן outside the מקדש, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but... (it is even forbidden)
Sacred offerings outside the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why at our סדר we lift the מצה and מרור when we explain them, but we do not lift the זרוע (shank bone).
steps.confusionAlert: 'אין צריך' here does not just mean 'optional'. The words 'ולא עוד אלא' show that lifting the meat is actually improper.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Matzah: one must lift it,
and bitter herbs: one must lift them.
Meat: one need not lift it.
And not only that, but
it looks like he is eating sacred offerings outside [the Temple].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second practical teaching from רבא about the explanation of פסח, מצה ומרור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lift the מצה and מרור. Do not lift the meat, so it does not look like קדשים eaten outside.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: a blind person is exempt from the הגדה
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב rules that a סומא (blind person) is exempt from saying the הגדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: a blind person is exempt from saying the הגדה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives a new rule: a blind person does not have to say the הגדה. The source for this comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the words 'מצה זו' and 'מרור זה', which involve pointing at the items. Someone who cannot see them cannot point to them, and that is the basis for the exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: Telling the story of יציאת מצרים

steps.confusionAlert: This is רב אחא's opinion. Right after this, the גמרא questions it, and in practice the הלכה is that a blind person does say the הגדה.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
A blind person is exempt from reciting the Haggadah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how to point at the items to whether someone who cannot see them is obligated at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סומא is exempt from the הגדה.

steps.title: The source: the word "this" links the הגדה to the בן סורר ומורה
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא's source is a word-link (גזירה שוה). The word 'זה' appears in the הגדה פסוק ('בעבור זה') and in the בן סורר ומורה פסוק ('בננו זה'). There, a blind parent is excluded, so here too a blind person is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written here: 'because of this', and it is written there: 'this son of ours'. Just as there it excludes a blind person, so too here it excludes blind people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רב אחא's rule comes from. It links two פסוקים that both use the word 'זה' (this).
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a בן סורר ומורה, the parents must say 'בננו זה', pointing to their son, so a blind parent who cannot point is excluded. Through the shared word 'זה', the same exclusion carries over to the הגדה, where we say 'בעבור זה' while pointing at the מצה and מרור.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here... and it is written there (a word-link)
Learning a law from a shared word in two פסוקים

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'זה' means pointing to something you can see. That is the basis for רב אחא's exemption of a סומא, though the גמרא will soon question it.

phrases.english: It is written here: 'because of this',
phrases.notes: שמות יג:ח, the source of the הגדה.

phrases.english: and it is written there: 'this son of ours'.
phrases.notes: דברים כא:כ, the בן סורר ומורה.

phrases.english: Just as there, it excludes a blind person,
so too here, it excludes blind people.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״בַּעֲבוּר זֶה״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״בְּנֵנוּ זֶה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק-based source for the ruling in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a סומא is exempt from the הגדה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה on the word 'זה': 'בעבור זה' (הגדה) and 'בננו זה' (בן סורר ומורה).

steps.title: Two blind sages said the הגדה themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב: מרימר reports that the blind אמוראים רב יוסף and רב ששת each said the הגדה in their own homes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But מרימר said: I asked the sages of רב יוסף's school, 'Who says the הגדה in רב יוסף's house?' They answered, 'רב יוסף himself.' I asked, 'Who says the הגדה in רב ששת's house?' They answered, 'רב ששת himself.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב אחא בר יעקב's ruling that a blind person is exempt. It points to two famous blind rabbis who led the הגדה themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רב יוסף and רב ששת were blind. If they said the הגדה for their households, they must have been obligated, because only someone who is obligated can fulfill the מצוה for others. That seems to contradict רב אחא בר יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (an opening word that signals a challenge)
מרימר, a later אמורא who asked about the practice
The הגדה, the telling of the Exodus story
The house or school of a rabbi

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'who said the הגדה' is not idle curiosity. מרימר is checking whether the blind sages relied on someone else, which would suggest they were exempt.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Mareimar say:
I asked the Sages of the school of Rav Yosef:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר אַגָּדְתָּא בֵּי רַב יוֹסֵף?
phrases.english: Who recites the Haggadah in Rav Yosef's house?
They said: Rav Yosef himself.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר אַגָּדְתָּא בֵּי רַב שֵׁשֶׁת?
phrases.english: Who recites the Haggadah in Rav Sheshet's house?
They said: Rav Sheshet himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 14 that a סומא is exempt.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's ruling that a blind person is exempt from the הגדה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Practice: two blind אמוראים led the הגדה for others, so they must have considered themselves obligated.

steps.title: Those sages hold מצה nowadays is rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף and רב ששת hold that מצה in our times is only a rabbinic obligation. So the Torah-based exemption for a blind person does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: These sages hold that מצה nowadays is only מדרבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רב יוסף and רב ששת are explained as holding that מצה today is only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה שוה from step 15 creates a Torah-level exemption. Without the קרבן פסח, these sages hold that מצה and the הגדה are only דרבנן, and they assume a Torah exemption need not carry over to a rabbinic מצוה. So a blind person is obligated, and they could lead the הגדה.

keyTerms.meaning: Nowadays, when there is no בית המקדש
A rabbinic obligation, not from the Torah

phrases.english: These Sages hold:
Matza nowadays is a rabbinic obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the level of obligation (Torah versus rabbinic).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The blind sages' practice contradicts the exemption.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption is Torah-level. These sages hold מצה today is rabbinic, so the exemption does not apply.

steps.title: But רב אחא בר יעקב also holds מצה is rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The answer implies that רב אחא בר יעקב holds מצה today is Torah-level. But he himself said it is rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רב אחא בר יעקב holds מצה nowadays is מדאורייתא? But it was רב אחא בר יעקב himself who said that מצה nowadays is מדרבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. That answer seems to clash with what we know רב אחא בר יעקב holds elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole disagreement is about Torah versus rabbinic, then רב אחא בר יעקב must hold מצה is Torah-level today. But we have a statement from him saying it is rabbinic. So why would he still exempt a blind person?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב סָבַר
phrases.english: Does this imply that Rav Acha bar Yaakov holds
that matza nowadays is a Torah obligation?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב הוּא דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: But Rav Acha bar Yaakov is the one who said:
Matza nowadays is rabbinic!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 17 by drawing out its implication.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the disagreement is about whether מצה today is Torah or rabbinic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction: רב אחא בר יעקב is on record holding מצה today is rabbinic, so that cannot be the difference between him and the blind sages.

steps.title: Rabbinic enactments follow the Torah's model
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב holds that whatever the רבנן enacted, they modeled on Torah law. So the Torah's exemption for a blind person carries over to the rabbinic מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that whatever the רבנן enacted, they enacted in the same pattern as Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רב אחא בר יעקב can hold that מצה is rabbinic and still exempt a blind person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא בר יעקב agrees the obligation today is דרבנן. But when the רבנן set up a מצוה to copy a Torah מצוה, they copied its rules as well. That includes the exemption for a סומא.

keyTerms.meaning: In the pattern of Torah law

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle 'כל דתקון רבנן כעין דאורייתא תקון' (rabbinic enactments mirror Torah law) appears in many places in ש״ס.

phrases.english: He holds: whatever the Sages enacted,
they enacted in the pattern of Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introducing a general principle that bridges Torah and rabbinic law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A rabbinic מצוה would not carry over a Torah exemption.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rabbinic enactments copy the Torah's rules, so the blind person's exemption still applies.

steps.title: Wouldn't the blind sages agree to that principle too?
steps.stepSummary: The principle that rabbinic enactments mirror Torah law is widely accepted. So רב ששת and רב יוסף should also hold a blind person exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב ששת and רב יוסף as well, surely whatever the רבנן enacted, they enacted in the pattern of Torah law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. If the principle is accepted, why did the blind sages not follow it and exempt themselves?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'הא ודאי' (surely) show this principle is not a private view of רב אחא בר יעקב. It is a basic rule everyone accepts. So the Torah/rabbinic distinction no longer explains the blind sages' practice, and we need a new explanation.

phrases.english: According to Rav Sheshet and Rav Yosef too,
surely whatever the Sages enacted
they enacted in the pattern of Torah law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle of step 19 back to the blind sages, which undoes the answer of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation of רב ששת and רב יוסף's practice as based on מצה being rabbinic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If rabbinic law mirrors Torah law for everyone, being rabbinic gives no reason to obligate a blind person.

steps.title: The word-link does not work: 'this' in the הגדה is needed
steps.stepSummary: The blind sages reject the גזירה שוה itself. In בן סורר ומורה, 'בננו זה' is extra wording that teaches pointing, which excludes blind parents. In the הגדה, 'בעבור זה' is necessary wording that refers to the מצה and מרור, so nothing is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? It makes sense there: the Torah could have written 'our son, he is,' yet it wrote 'this son of ours.' So we learn that the word is there to exclude blind parents. But here, if not 'because of this,' what else could the Torah write? So the word is there to refer to the מצה and מרור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason for the blind sages' practice. They never accepted רב אחא בר יעקב's source, so a blind person is obligated even on a Torah level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word can only teach a special law if it is extra. In בן סורר ומורה, 'זה' replaced the simpler 'הוא,' so it teaches that the parents must point at their son, which a blind parent cannot do. In the הגדה, 'זה' is the normal way to say 'because of these foods,' so it teaches nothing extra. The word-link falls apart, and there is no exemption to copy.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)
'This son of ours,' from the פסוק of בן סורר ומורה
'Because of this,' from the הגדה פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: רב אחא בר יעקב exempts a סומא based on the word 'זה.' He holds that even today's rabbinic הגדה copies that Torah exemption. רב יוסף and רב ששת obligate a סומא, because in the הגדה the word 'זה' is simply needed to point to the מצה and מרור. So no exemption is derived from it.
steps.confusionAlert: The final answer does not say the blind sages reject 'כל דתקון רבנן כעין דאורייתא תקון.' They accept it. They reject the exemption at its root, in the Torah פסוק itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows a key rule of דרשה: a word can only teach something new when it is extra. Wording that is needed for the plain meaning cannot carry an added teaching.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
It makes sense there,
since the verse could have written 'our son, he is,'
and instead it is written 'this son of ours,'

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: פְּרָט לְסוֹמִין הוּא דַּאֲתָא.
phrases.english: learn from it: it comes to exclude blind parents.
But here, if not 'because of this,'
what else could it write?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בַּעֲבוּר מַצָּה וּמָרוֹר הוּא דַּאֲתָא.
phrases.english: Rather, it comes to say 'because of matza and maror.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by rejecting the גזירה שוה of step 15 for the view of רב ששת and רב יוסף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the source: the key word is necessary in one פסוק and extra in the other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both appearances of 'זה' teach the same thing, so a blind person is exempt from the הגדה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the extra 'זה' in בן סורר ומורה excludes the blind. The 'זה' of the הגדה is needed for its plain meaning, so a blind person is obligated.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יוסף and רב ששת hold a blind person is obligated in the הגדה, because the word-link that רב אחא בר יעקב relies on does not work.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: Therefore we are obligated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה, 'לפיכך אנחנו חייבים,' to open a new topic.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: Therefore we are obligated (to thank and praise).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finished with the blind-person discussion and now quotes a new line from the משנה. This is a setup line that opens the next discussion. It is not a ruling of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, 'לפיכך' (therefore) follows the teaching that every person must see himself as if he personally left מצרים. Because of that, we are obligated to give thanks and praise, which leads into saying הלל. By quoting these words, the גמרא marks which part of the משנה it is about to discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore. It links our duty to praise to what came just before it in the משנה: seeing ourselves as if we left מצרים.
We are obligated. It shows that thanking and praising at the סדר is a real requirement, not just a nice extra.
To thank and to praise. These are the words in the משנה that follow 'לפיכך אנחנו חייבים.'

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement by an אמורא. It is just the גמרא quoting the משנה as a heading, the way a commentary quotes the words it is about to explain.

phrases.english: Therefore we are obligated (to thank and praise).
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה as a heading for the discussion that follows.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה (only if one reads the quote as the start of a question about this line)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off the blind-person discussion (Steps 14–21) and returns to the text of the משנה to start a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because each person must see himself as if he left מצרים, we are obligated to thank and praise ה'. This is the opening of the הלל section of the סדר.
